body.statement:
Suppose \(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0\le1/2\).  For every \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) there are constants \(c_\alpha>0\) and \(\eta_\alpha>2\alpha\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(T\), the base Holder model class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) contains two laws with the same interior realized path whose observed-data laws possess a common subprobability measure of mass at least \(\eta_\alpha\), while their causal targets differ by at least
\[
 c_\alpha\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\]
Both laws satisfy the frozen geometric beta-mixing envelope and the design-conditional centering assumption.  No lower local-modulus condition is used.
body.justification: The rare-cluster construction has a common treated mean and directly certifies the geometric-mixing spacing penalty.
body.gap: Independent-design spacing alone does not cover triangular-array clustering.
body.consumer: Marginal and honest-length lower bounds use its common-submeasure certificate.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(q=Sd\).  Since \(B^4\ge q^2\), the common donor law
\(Z_j=z_0+U_j\), with independent Rademacher coordinates in \(U_j\), has mean \(z_0\), covariance \(I_q\), and
\(\mathbb E\|U_j\|_2^4=q^2\).  Take it independent of the complete joint panel.

Choose \(\gamma>0\) so small that \(e^{-\gamma}>2\alpha\), and define
\[
 L_T=\left\lfloor
 \frac{\log T-2\log\log(T\vee3)}{|\log\rho_0|}
 \right\rfloor\vee1,
 \qquad p_T=\frac{\gamma L_T}{T}.                             \tag{1}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}.                               \tag{2}
\]
Partition the first cohort's calendar into complete consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\).  Independently label each complete block by
\(C_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Let \(A_T\) be a cube centered at \(z_{01}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_d\) with volume \(p_T\).  Conditional on \(C_b=1\), draw all design points in the block independently uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(C_b=0\), draw them independently uniformly on \(A_T^c\).  At every date in a complete block the marginal density equals
\[
 p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
 +(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1                 \tag{3}
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\).  Draw the incomplete block and all other cohorts independently and uniformly, so the fixed-query density bounds hold.

For a lag \(k<L_T\), past and future sigma-fields separated by \(k\) dates share at most one Bernoulli block label.  Couple one copy by replacing that shared label on the future side with an independent copy.  The mismatch probability is
\(2p_T(1-p_T)\le2p_T\), which bounds the absolute-regularity coefficient.  If \(k\ge L_T\), the sigma-fields use disjoint independent labels and the coefficient is zero.  Since \(\rho_0^k\ge\rho_0^{L_T-1}\) for \(k<L_T\), (2) gives
\[
 \beta(k)\le2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}
 \le\beta_0\rho_0^k.                                        \tag{4}
\]

Let \(E_T\) be the event that every complete-block label is zero and that no point in the incomplete block lies in a fixed smaller concentric cube.  The incomplete-block failure probability is at most \(L_Tp_T=o(1)\), whereas
\[
 \Pr(E_T)=(1-p_T)^{\lfloor T/L_T\rfloor}-o(1)
 \longrightarrow e^{-\gamma}>
 \eta_\alpha:=\frac{e^{-\gamma}+2\alpha}{2}>2\alpha.        \tag{5}
\]
Let \(h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\) be the side scale of the smaller cube.  Define
\[
 \phi(u)=\prod_{k=1}^{d}\psi(u_k),\qquad
 \psi(v)=
 \begin{cases}
  \exp\{1-(1-v^2)^{-1}\},&|v|<1,\\
 0,&|v|\ge1.
 \end{cases}
\]
After a fixed rescaling its support lies in the smaller cube.  For sufficiently small fixed \(a,b_0>0\), put
\[
 m_{10}(x)=b_0,\qquad
 m_{11}(x)=b_0+ah_T^\lambda\phi((x-z_{01})/h_T),              \tag{6}
\]
and keep other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).  A derivative of order \(j\le\lfloor\lambda\rfloor\) of the perturbation is bounded by a constant times \(h_T^{\lambda-j}\), and its top-order Holder seminorm is uniformly bounded.  Thus fixed small \(a\) places both surfaces in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and small \(a,b_0\) enforce boundedness.

Under alternative \(v\), set \(Q_{1ti}=m_{1v}(X_{1t})\), use the common constant surfaces elsewhere, and take the same positive constant treated observation for every replica.  The latter verifies common treated-mean replication and design invariance.  Impose consistency and set untreated event wealth equal to \(m_{sv}(z_{0s})\).  Baseline wealth one, horizon-zero return equal to wealth minus one, and later returns zero realize the buy-and-hold levels.  Conditional centering is exact; conditional on the design, histories are degenerate and hence mutually independent.  Equations (3)--(4) verify query-conditional design regularity, and the donors satisfy all donor conditions.  Both laws are in the panel class and their labelled kernels are in the same fixed-query class.

On \(E_T\), no response is evaluated in the bump support.  The restrictions of the two observed laws to \(E_T\) coincide, giving a common subprobability measure of mass at least \(\eta_\alpha\) for sufficiently large \(T\).  Finally, Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (6) yield
\[
 |\tau_1(z_0)-\tau_0(z_0)|
 =\pi_1ah_T^\lambda
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}. \tag{7}
\]
This proves the required common-submeasure certificate.
